features.name: argument_exceeds_100_words
features.definition: Does the original argument contain more than one hundred words?
features.spec: If df['argument'] is missing/non-string, return null. Otherwise count words as len(str(argument).split()) (whitespace-separated tokens, raw current text including any edits or outcome announcements). Return 1 if count > 100, else 0 (empty string gives 0 words -> 0).

h0: There is no difference in the likelihood of view change between discussions where `argument_exceeds_100_words` is 1 and those where it is 0.
h1: Discussions with `argument_exceeds_100_words` equal to 1 have a lower likelihood of view change than those with 0.
note: Word count uses whitespace tokenization of the current argument text only (title excluded). The text may contain edits or view-change announcements, so it is not guaranteed to be the initial argument; this mechanical count is not filtered. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; the association is not causal.
